Do you remember the feeling the first time you backed out of your parents' driveway? That feeling was pure freedom. But for your parents, that moment may have been one of the scariest of their lives. When you were a teenager, your parents had absolutely no way of knowing if you were speeding, where you went, when you arrived, or how safely you were driving. No news was good news, and until you called to check in, hope was all they had to rely on.

If you now have a teenager who drives, consider yourself lucky, because in this day and age, you no longer have to endure the same kind of unknown fear that the previous generation of parents experienced. Technology in 2026 has plenty of drawbacks, but HeyPolo is a perfect example of how technology can make the lives of teenage drivers better and safer.

HeyPolo is much more than just a paid version of Apple's "Find My" service.

HeyPolo is a family safety app that, for one price, includes real-time location sharing, arrival and departure notifications, SOS emergency alerts, and driving safety features. These driving features are precisely what set it apart from typical location-sharing apps (such as Apple's "Find My"). Every single trip your teenage driver takes is recorded and scored, so you can clearly see the details of the journey: how fast they were going, whether they used their phone while driving, whether there was any hard braking or sudden acceleration, and whether any serious driving incidents were detected.

"Driving Scores" rate every trip based on actual driving behaviour, so you'll never have to guess whether your son or daughter is really driving safely. You can see the data, and if their performance isn't up to scratch, you can have a serious talk with them. As their habits improve, you'll see the scores gradually rise. Compared with anything the previous generation had access to, this is a far more practical way to help new-licence drivers improve their driving skills.

Collision detection, arrival alerts, and more handy features

HeyPolo automatically detects collisions and notifies you. Combined with arrival alerts, whether your kids are heading back to school, going to sports practice, hanging out with friends, or coming home, you can move from simply hoping "no news is good news" to actually knowing whether they're safe. You no longer have to wait for them to arrive before texting or calling them; the moment they get there, you'll know, and that kind of peace of mind for parents is truly priceless. HeyPolo updates every 5 seconds, so your location information is always accurate.

One price, covers the whole family

A single HeyPolo subscription covers your entire family, with absolutely no extra per-person fees. It works flawlessly whether you use an iPhone or Android, so it's fine to have a mix of devices at home. HeyPolo was developed by the team behind Surfshark, which means they have a very solid privacy infrastructure backing them. They won't sell your data, you control who you share with, how much you share, and when you stop sharing, and all data is deleted every 7 days. For a location-centric app, this is extremely important when it comes to privacy.

HeyPolo offers a 30-day money-back guarantee. If you and your family try it out and feel it's not right for you, there are no binding contracts either, so there's absolutely no reason not to give it a try.

Through the link below, 9to5Mac readers can subscribe to HeyPolo at 33% off, which means the monthly fee works out to just US$3.99 per year on average for the whole household.
